draft.title: Hatshepsut's family background
card: Hatshepsut lived in Egypt's 18th Dynasty, in the New Kingdom. She was the daughter of the pharaoh Thutmose I and his queen, Ahmose.
She married her half-brother, Thutmose II, who became pharaoh after their father. This made her the king's wife, with the title Great Royal Wife.
When Thutmose II died, his son Thutmose III was still a young child. He was born to a lesser wife, not to Hatshepsut.
Hatshepsut became regent. A regent runs the government for a king who is too young to rule. She was Thutmose III's stepmother and aunt, so she was closely related to him.
draft.remember: Hatshepsut was a pharaoh's daughter and a pharaoh's wife, and she ruled for a boy king as regent.

a.q: What was Hatshepsut's role when she acted as regent for Thutmose III?
opts: She ran the government because he was too young
She shared the throne with him as an equal king
She ruled Egypt because he had been removed
She ruled after his death until another king came
a.why: A regent governs for a king who is too young to rule. Thutmose III was a young child, so he was still the king. The option about sharing the throne as an equal king describes a later stage, not the role of a regent.
a.clue: Think about why a young child could not run the country.

b.q: Which statement correctly describes Hatshepsut's family links before she became regent?
opts: She was Thutmose I's daughter and Thutmose II's wife
She was Thutmose II's daughter and Thutmose III's wife
She was Thutmose III's mother and Thutmose I's wife
She was Thutmose I's wife and Thutmose II's mother
b.why: Hatshepsut was born to Thutmose I, then married her half-brother Thutmose II. Thutmose III was Thutmose II's son by a lesser wife, so he was not her child, which rules out the option that makes her his mother.
b.clue: Start with her father, then her husband.

a.best: She ran the government because he was too young

b.best: She was Thutmose I's daughter and Thutmose II's wife
